rows.whatChanged: ONE RULE IN ONE TABLE IN ONE FILE, PLUS ITS DISCLOSURE. In scripts/build-census-v1-tx_nd_conviction_no_supervision-set.mjs the SOI_RULES rule `declaration_date` matched /^(Day \/ Día|Month \/ Mes|Year \/ Año|Today|Year)$/ and called all five a date part of the sworn declaration, refused because 'a date written before the Statement is actually sworn would be false'. That reason is exactly right for the day the participant signs and exactly wrong for the day they were born. The rule is narrowed to /^(Today|Year)$/ and two rules are added ahead of it. THE THREE FIELDS AND THEIR NEW DISPOSITIONS: (1) 'Month / Mes' -- was PROTECTED_FIELD, class signature_or_date_participant_completion, printedLabel 'Date part of the sworn declaration (Month / Mes)'; is now REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, requiredBeforeFiling true, disclosureLabel 'Month box of the date of birth on the Option 1 declaration, page 11', printedLabel 'My date of birth is / Mi fecha de nacimiento es'. (2) 'Day / Día' -- same before; now REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, disclosureLabel 'Date-of-birth box on the Option 1 declaration, page 11 (Day / Día)', same printed caption. (3) 'Year / Año' -- same before; now REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, disclosureLabel 'Date-of-birth box on the Option 1 declaration, page 11 (Year / Año)', same printed caption. Each carries its own reason naming the two-widget fact. WHAT STAYS REFUSED, unchanged in label, class and reason: the signing-date field 'Today' at (97.75,302.31) on source page 11, and the notary's 'Year' at (343.359,264.575) on source page 12. Both remain PROTECTED_FIELD under signature_or_date_participant_completion with the reason that was always true of them. THE CAPTION IS THE FORM'S. statementFields() now passes a rule's `caption` and `captionAt` through to the census row, so the three rows carry the line the paper actually prints and censusOf's captionDrift check re-reads page 11 of the pinned binary on every build; a caption that moved or was reworded fails the build. captionDrift is empty on both builds. THE DISCLOSURE. The three blanks are named in participant-instructions.md at lines 113, 138 and 174 of 'The items you must supply', each with what to write; a line naming all three by their printed caption is added to 'Things the platform deliberately left blank'; and the sentence describing what the platform filled in now says the Statement asks for the date of birth twice and points at that section. One paragraph naming the three boxes is also added to the delivered filing-and-after-order-instructions component. THE PRECEDENT. This is not a new treatment invented here. The identical structure on the identical pinned Statement of Inability -- TX__STATEMENTOFINABILITYTOAFFORDPAYMENTOFCOURTCOSTSO.pdf, sha256 bd17a3fe43d6989d1828c91c9a46c873908c272d8e2e342af35ce8bdb2fab10d -- was treated exactly this way by FIX29 in scripts/build-census-v1-rcap-tx-custom-pleading.mjs, whose rules option1_date_of_birth_month and option1_date_of_birth_day_and_year this lane mirrors down to the caption and captionAt. VF01 tested the two-widget claim against the pinned binary, accepted that treatment on 2026-09-05, and that family passed a fresh read at 321938c38. This family follows it rather than inventing a second answer to the same form.

whyDeclaredAndNotWritten.measuredHere: Read with pdf-lib from the pinned binary in this container, not taken from the precedent's word for it.
whyDeclaredAndNotWritten.provedByExperiment: setText('04') on 'Month / Mes', updateFieldAppearances, flatten, save; pdftotext -f 12 -l 12 -layout on the result prints '04' directly under 'Juramentado y suscrito ante mí el día de hoy del mes de'. The probe file was written to /tmp and deleted.
whyDeclaredAndNotWritten.whyTheFactoryCannotWriteOneWidget: scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs holds one value per FIELD, not per widget, and says so at its fitting step: 'a field holds one value however many places it is printed.' Its three widget-aware options -- fitTextPerWidget, applyPerWidgetDefaultAppearanceSizes and alignWidgetDefaultAppearanceSizes -- all concern SIZE, not value. Writing the participant's birth month would therefore print it in the notary's blank on a page the notary completes.
whyDeclaredAndNotWritten.whyNotWriteTheOtherTwo: Two of the three boxes could be written and the third could not. A date that is two-thirds machine-filled on a declaration sworn under penalty of perjury is a worse artifact than one the participant completes in one hand, and the completeness contract reads a written cell beside a required blank cell in the same row as an incomplete row. All three are declared together.
whyDeclaredAndNotWritten.whyThisIsNotAnUnavailableFactRefusedAsAv: REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING_CONDITIONS asks whether the fact is genuinely unavailable, and the honest answer for this blank is that the platform's INK cannot reach it, not that the value is unknown. The row does not claim otherwise: factAvailable is not asserted, factId is null, and the reason on every one of the three rows names the two-widget fact rather than pleading ignorance of the date. The participant is told, in the same sentence, that the date they need is already printed nine pages earlier on page 2 of the same document, so the disclosure hands them the value rather than asking them to find it. This is the reading VF01 accepted on the same form on 2026-09-05.
whyDeclaredAndNotWritten.whatARealWriteWouldHaveNeeded: A per-widget value facility in the shared finalizer, opt-in and default-off in the pattern of fitTextPerWidget, plus date-part addressing that scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-field-semantics.mjs currently refuses for bare date-component field names and that scripts/rcap-official-forms/verify-name-date-component-semantics.mjs holds in place across every committed census. That is a shared-machinery change touching roughly 250 families and it is not what the accepted precedent does.
